methodology.method_family: mini review with proposed evaluation framework
methodology.technology_context: generative AI, large language models (GPT-4, Med-PaLM, Claude), AI chatbots, patient-facing digital health tools

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a peer-reviewed mini review on generative AI and LLM-based patient-facing tools in consumer health, proposing the RECAP evaluation framework for safety, usability, and effectiveness. It is relevant to regulated conversational AI governance, but the provided text shows a conceptual/framework contribution rather than primary empirical governance implementation or operational controls.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only partial front matter and early sections were provided; full-text screening should verify review methods, limitations, and whether operational governance mechanisms beyond the RECAP framework are discussed.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is based only on the excerpt provided. The paper clearly states it is a mini review and proposes the RECAP framework, but the supplied text does not describe systematic search, inclusion criteria, or full limitations.

cerqual.explanation: The framework is clearly articulated and directly addresses LLM/chatbot use in regulated consumer health, but confidence is moderated because the excerpt lacks detail on review methodology, evidence selection, and stated limitations.

coding.theme: Evaluation framework for generative AI in consumer health
coding.subtheme: Clinical safety and responsible implementation of LLM chatbots
rq_alignment: governance of generative AI in regulated settings

synthesis.main_claim: Generative AI powered by LLMs can improve consumer health literacy and personalized education, but responsible patient-facing deployment requires a robust digital health framework; the authors propose the RECAP model to evaluate relevance, evidence-base, clarity, adaptability, and precision.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a clinician-informed conceptual lens (RECAP) and contextualizes promises and pitfalls of LLM/chatbot use cases in consumer health, including mental health and lifestyle guidance.
synthesis.limitations: The provided excerpt does not report systematic review methods, sample/search strategy, or comprehensive limitations; only partial text was available for appraisal.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence for governance-oriented evaluation frameworks in regulated healthcare conversational AI, especially for safety, ethics, and oversight of chatbots and patient-facing LLM tools.

evidence.claim: Study type is a mini review proposing an evaluation framework.
evidence.excerpt: This mini review examines current use cases for generative AI in consumer health education, highlights persistent challenges, and proposes a clinician-informed framework to evaluate safety, usability, and effectiveness.

evidence.claim: Article focuses on specific LLMs in healthcare communication.
evidence.excerpt: LLMs, including OpenAI’s Generative Pre-trained Transformer 4 (GPT-4), Google’s Med-PaLM, and Anthropic’s Claude, are trained on extensive internet and medical text.

evidence.claim: Authors propose the RECAP governance/evaluation model.
evidence.excerpt: The RECAP model—Relevance, Evidence-based, Clarity, Adaptability, and Precision—offers a pragmatic lens to guide responsible implementation of AI in patient-facing tools.

evidence.claim: Clinical safety and risk concerns are central motivations.
evidence.excerpt: However, ensuring clinical safety and effectiveness requires a robust digital health framework to address risks like misinformation and inequitable communication.

evidence.claim: Conversational AI/chatbots are explicit use cases.
evidence.excerpt: AI chatbots, software applications that use artiﬁcial intelligence to simulate human conversation, can simplify complex terminology and generate personalized responses to common health questions.
evidence.section: 2.1 Health literacy and generative AI chatbots

evidence.claim: Oversight is needed for unpredictable generative conversational tools.
evidence.excerpt: Yet, unlike structured CBT apps like Woebot or Wysa, generative models are more unpredictable and require careful oversight to avoid unintentional reinforcement of maladaptive behaviors
